description: Looping random sequencer built on a 16-bit shift register, with a voltage sequence and a gate output taken from the first bit

params.text: While it is held, the first bit of the shift register is set to zero on each clock pulse, turning ones into zeroes
While it is held, the first bit of the shift register is set to one on each clock pulse, turning zeroes into ones
Sets the chance the last bit is inverted as it is copied back to the first: even at the centre, none at L so the loop repeats unaltered, and inversion every time round at C, doubling the loop
Sets the bit the sequence is copied back from, 1 to 16, which is the length of the loop

inputs.text: Each rising edge moves the shift register on by one bit; it counts as high from 2V upwards
Modulates SHIFT, BITS or the sequence level, whichever the menu has assigned; assigned to the level, the voltage here sets the range of SEQ outright, and SEQ rests at 0V while this jack is empty

outputs.text: The first eight bits of the shift register read as a number from 0 to 255 and scaled to a range of 8V, giving a new voltage on every clock pulse
Carries 8V while the first bit of the shift register is a one, for as long as the clock pulse lasts

notes: the contents of the shift register are saved with the patch, so a locked sequence comes back when the patch is reopened
the module has no clock of its own and no step button; nothing changes until a clock is patched to CLOCK
menu: Control input — chooses Shift, Bits or Level for what the CTRL jack modulates
